subject: ela
intro: Eleventh graders determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; they provide an objective summary. Complex informational texts carry several intertwined central ideas.

items.prompt:
Read.

The automobile gave Americans unprecedented freedom and mobility, but it also reshaped cities around cars and worsened pollution.

Name TWO central ideas and how they interact.

steps: One: the car expanded freedom/mobility. Two: it reshaped cities and harmed the environment.
They interact: the same freedom drove the sprawl and pollution.
So the benefit and the costs are linked by the same cause.
solution.answer: The car's freedom/mobility and its costs (sprawl, pollution); the benefit caused the costs.

steps: State the central ideas without opinion.
So: 'The automobile expanded freedom and mobility while reshaping cities around cars and worsening pollution.'
solution.answer: 'The automobile expanded freedom and mobility while reshaping cities and worsening pollution.'

items.prompt: How do two central ideas INTERACT?

steps: They can reinforce, complicate, or qualify one another.
So they build a more complex overall analysis.
solution.answer: They reinforce or complicate one another to build a complex analysis.

items.prompt: A complex text may carry ____ central ideas.
An opinion-free retelling is an ____ summary.
Two central ideas can ____ one another.
